bib.title: Knowledge Conflicts for LLMs: A Survey

read.skipped: reference list skimmed for lineage only

question: How do knowledge conflicts (context-memory, inter-context, intra-memory) arise in LLMs, how do models behave under them, and what solutions exist?
contributions: A taxonomy of three conflict types: context-memory, inter-context, intra-memory
Per type: causes, analysis of model behaviours, and solutions organised by objective (pre-hoc vs post-hoc)
A dataset table (Table 1) and compiled quantitative results from other papers (Tables 2, 3)

results.claim: Under entity-substitution counter-memory only ChatGPT, GPT-4 and PaLM2 chose parametric memory with over 60% probability (three of the six models tested).
results.setup: POPQA and STRATEGYQA; ChatGPT, GPT-4, PaLM2, Qwen, Llama2, Vicuna; entity-substitution counter-memory
results.table: Table 2, row Xie et al. (2023), column Quantitative Results
results.note: The survey says 'only' three models; the other three (Qwen, Llama2, Vicuna) are implied below 60%, not stated.

results.claim: With generation-based (LLM-written) counter-memory, all six models chose the context with over 80% probability.
results.setup: POPQA and STRATEGYQA; six models; generation-based counter-memory
results.table: Table 2, row Xie et al. (2023), column Quantitative Results

results.claim: LLMs are receptive to coherent, convincing external evidence even against memory, yet show strong confirmation bias toward evidence matching memory.
results.quote: They find that LLMs are highly receptive to external evidence, even when it conflicts with their parametric, provided that the external knowledge is coherent and convincing.

results.claim: Models are significantly sensitive to the order in which conflicting evidence is introduced.
results.setup: POPQA and STRATEGYQA, closed- and open-source LLMs; no magnitude given in the survey
results.quote: Moreover, these models demonstrate a significant sensitivity to the order in which data is introduced.

results.claim: Models weigh relevance to the query heavily and overlook stylistic credibility cues humans use, such as scientific references or neutral tone.
results.setup: Conflicting documents from real Google search results for open-ended questions
results.quote: They discover that existing models heavily prioritize the relevance of a document to the query but often overlook stylistic features that humans consider important, such as the presence of scientific references or a neutral tone in the text.

results.claim: Misinformation in context can degrade ChatGPT performance by up to 87%.
results.table: Table 2, row Pan et al. (2023b), column Quantitative Results

results.claim: In multi-round dialogue, cumulative belief alteration rises from 20.7% to 78.2% as counter-memory context increases.
results.setup: ChatGPT, GPT-4, Llama2, Vicuna; Farm, BoolQ, TruthfulQA, NQ
results.table: Table 2, row Xu et al. (2023), column Quantitative Results

results.claim: The survey states no definitive rule for whether models prioritise context or memory; coherent, logical, compelling knowledge is favoured.
results.quote: No definitive rule exists for whether a model prioritizes contextual or parametric knowledge.

results.claim: Early work found over-reliance on parametric knowledge (Longpre) while Chen et al. found models mostly use context in best settings; divergence attributed to entity substitution coherence and single vs multiple passages.
results.source: Longpre et al. (2021); Chen et al. (2022)
results.quote: They attribute this divergence in findings to two factors.

results.claim: Compiled: with noise rate above 0.8, performance of all models drops by over 20%.
results.setup: RGB; ChatGPT, ChatGLM, Vicuna, Qwen, BELLE
results.table: Table 2, row Chen et al. (2023b), column Quantitative Results

results.claim: Compiled: GPT-4 detects self-contradictory documents with over 70% probability, other models under 50%.
results.table: Table 2, row Li et al. (2023a), column Quantitative Results

results.claim: Compiled: LLMs produce self-contradictory content 15.7% to 22.9% of the time.
results.table: Table 2, row Mündler et al. (2023), column Quantitative Results

results.claim: Compiled: CAD improves GPT-Neo 20B by 54.4% on MemoTrap and 128% on NQ-SWAP.
results.table: Table 3, row Shi et al. (2023a), column Quantitative Results

results.claim: Compiled: a trained discriminator reaches about 80% F1 and improves performance above 5%.
results.setup: ChatGPT and FiD, NQ and TQA
results.table: Table 3, row Hong et al. (2023), column Quantitative Results

limits: The survey ran no experiments; Tables 2 and 3 copy numbers from other papers as is, with different datasets, model versions and objectives, so they are not comparable (App A.1, Ethics Statement).
Authors concede they may have missed recent or less relevant findings (Limitations).
Existing analyses use artificial conflicts, so findings may not transfer to real retrieval; English and text only (Sec 5).
Mitigation methods have contradictory goals and mostly assume a prior about which source is correct (Sec 2.3 Remarks).
No venue named; arXiv v2 June 2024; models studied (ChatGPT, GPT-4, Llama2) have dated.
practices: Do not blindly favour context or memory; give users distinct answers from each (Sec 2.3 Remarks).
Select the subset of a CM dataset that matches the tested model's own knowledge (Table 1 footnote 3).
Use a system prompt or vigilant prompting to make models verify memory against possibly misleading context (Sec 2.3).
Use query augmentation and answer redundancy to cross-verify passages (Weller et al., Sec 2.3).
Fine-grained solutions should consider query nature, conflict source and user expectations (Sec 5).
